newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel firmer in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel firmer in thin trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil market rose further on Tuesday after putting on about 30 cents a day earlier as buyers extended their support in thin trading as sellers retreated to a higher level, traders said.
They said an offer late Monday at $21.50 per barrel free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis attracted a buyer but the two parties could not agree on operational terms.
The offered level was 30 cents above Monday's highest traded level.
On Monday, four cargoes totalling 670,000 barrels in four cargoes traded at between $20.90 and $21.20 per barrel.
Cuts in refinery runs in Singapore, maintenance shutdowns in Indonesia and reverse arbitrage exports from the region to the West were cited for the renewed optimism.
But others said the absence of China in the spot market is still a source of concern.
China had in the second quarter halved its diesel imports from about two million in the first quarter, traders said.
They said demand in the third quarter is also low due to high stocks.
The jet fuel market was steady and remained well supported by a Singapore trader.
The trader bought a 180,000-barrel cargo from a European major at $23.40 and was still seeking to buy another 100,000 barrels at the same level.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp has issued a tender to buy 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel for September 1-20 delivery, cost-and-freight Keelung or Shenao.
The tender closes on July 30 and offers are valid for two days.
